marquee.headline: Half your repeat revenue comes from 12% of first orders. Which 12%?
paragraphs: You know your repeat rate. You do not know who is in it. You find out ninety days late, when the second order does not arrive.

Northquay reads your order history and scores every first-time buyer on day two: coming back, or already gone. It sits on Shopify and Klaviyo, so the answer turns into a flow instead of a slide nobody acts on.
bullets: A repeat-purchase score on every customer by day two
Cohorts split by first product, discount and acquisition channel
The real reorder window for each SKU, measured rather than assumed
Scores pushed into Klaviyo as segments, hourly
marquee.offer: Workspace6 members get 90 days free and a teardown of their last twelve months of cohorts.

shoutout.text: Your repeat rate is a fact about last year. Northquay turns it into a list of names: which first-time buyers will reorder, scored two days after they order, synced into Klaviyo. One skincare brand found 14% of first orders drove 61% of year-two revenue, then built a flow around exactly those people.

welcome.headline: Most brands find out a customer is gone ninety days after they left.
paragraphs: Northquay is retention analytics for DTC brands. It reads your order history and scores every first-time buyer on how likely they are to come back, two days after their first order.
That score lands in Klaviyo as a segment, so the people worth chasing get chased and the rest stop costing you discount codes.
